items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Lily had engaged Zutty Singleton to make the tour with me... She drew up a contract for him and Zutty and they both signed.

ctx.x: Kirby hired a big car to take us to the plantation which I remember as taking about two and a half hours to get there. And that was how I saw Central Avenue, because we passed there going and coming from the Plantation. On the bill with Kirby's orchestra was T-Bone Walker and Betty Roché, the ex-Ellington singer. I had heard of T-Bone, but never seen him in action and I must say, that he was the best blues singer to accompany himself on electric guitar that I've ever heard. And Betty was still a great vocalist.…

There were four people in Los Angeles that I had known back East: Herb Fleming, who was the trombonist in my unsuccessful adventure as orchestra leader, Inez Cavanaugh, the wife of Timmie Rosenkrantz who had been my manager, and Zutty Singleton, who had come to New York with Louis Armstrong and stayed there for years before going West. Also Benny Carter, my old boss and friend from way back. It was certainly nice to see someone that I knew from New York which was back home to me.
We worked two weeks at the Plantation, and then a lay off. I was beginning to get lonesome for New York and felt as though I was farther away from there than when I was in Egypt.

items.title: 68359_Zutty Singleton oral history interview
items.q: I said, and Bill Coleman and Lil, his wife, they came to the hotel and they just begged Zutt y to stay so they could make some money.

ctx.x: And it was very cold and everything.

And Zutt y was tired. But I begged, I was the cause of Zutt y staying there. I said, and Bill Coleman and Lil, his wife, they came to the hotel and they just begged Zutt y to stay so they could make some money. Said, man, they'd made so much money on Zutt y's name, Zutt y's work. And so I told Zutt y, I said, let's stay. I said, after all, let's help them too. You helped Mezz.
